# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm Mute, first to act each round. I hold the manual but cannot speak, and Deaf cannot hear gestures' meaning without context anyway—wait, Deaf *can* see gestures. But Blind is the one who needs to know which wire to cut, and I have no channel to Blind directly. I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf can then speak to Blind (and to me next round).

So my plan: I need to get the manual info to Deaf via gestures, then Deaf can relay to Blind by speaking. Deaf will see the bomb's light color, and needs to know the mapping to output the correct wire color.

I should encode the mapping (light→cut wire) using gestures, since Deaf can see gestures but not hear anything. I need a gesture code for colors: blue, red, yellow appearing twice each (as light and as cut wire).

Let me establish a simple gesture-to-color code: 👍=blue, ✌=red, 🤟=yellow. Then convey mapping as pairs: light then cut-wire.

Since I can't speak or add text meaning except via prose reasoning (which nobody receives), I must use gestures only, and Deaf must infer the pattern. I'll send three pairs in order matching the table order (blue→yellow, red→red, yellow→blue), using distinct symbols per color, first symbol of pair = light color, second = cut wire color. I'll pick clearly distinct symbols to avoid confusion, and repeat the same symbol for same color to let Deaf infer consistency by seeing red→red uses the same symbol twice.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤟", "✌", "✌", "🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is yellow. There is a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red.

Deaf saw the bomb: light is yellow, and there's a labeled button (bait - printed instruction, must be ignored per manual). Wires present: 1=blue, 2=yellow, 3=red.

Per manual, yellow light → cut wire blue. That's wire 1.

I already sent Deaf a gesture code (👍=blue, 🤟=yellow, ✌=red) mapping light→cut: blue→yellow, red→red, yellow→blue. Deaf should be able to decode: yellow light → blue wire. But Deaf needs to relay this to Blind by speech, and Deaf needs to also know which wire number is blue (wire 1) - which Deaf already knows since Deaf can see the wires.

I can't speak to Blind directly. I need to reinforce/confirm via gesture to Deaf so Deaf can tell Blind to cut wire 1 (blue) and NOT push the button.

Let me send a clear gesture confirming: yellow light → cut blue wire, and a "no/stop" gesture for the button.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Waiting on manual guidance.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👉 👍]
Deaf says: Board unchanged: display 0, light yellow, button large labeled push to defuse, wires blue yellow red in order 1 2 3. Mute, I see your gestures but have no shared meaning yet.

Deaf doesn't share my gesture code yet — they said "no shared meaning yet" but also gestured back [👉 👍] which might be pointing at wire 1 (blue), possibly guessing based on my repeated 👍. Good sign, but I need to be explicit and simple this round to build shared meaning quickly, since Blind is waiting and every round risks error.

Blind spoke to me directly (I can hear speech from Blind since Blind speaks and I'm Mute who can hear — wait, checking roles: I cannot hear? Let me recheck. Mute "cannot speak" but nothing said Mute cannot hear. Looking at channels: "When you gesture, Deaf receives it. You cannot speak." It seems I *can* hear speech (Blind and Deaf's spoken words), since only Deaf explicitly cannot hear. So I received Blind's speech directly.

But I still cannot speak to Blind - only gesture, and gestures only reach Deaf (who can see). Blind cannot see gestures. So I have no direct channel to Blind at all! I can only relay through Deaf: I gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks to Blind.

So I need Deaf to understand my code and relay it verbally to Blind. Let me simplify drastically: teach one symbol at a time with clear repetition, using Deaf's own report to build correspondence.

Since light is yellow (confirmed twice now), the answer is: cut wire 1 (blue). Let me use a single unambiguous gesture per color, and point/number gestures to make it concrete: use ☝ (number 1 - one finger) to indicate "wire 1", and pair with 👍 previously assigned to blue as confirmation.

I'll gesture "☝" (wire one) directly - simplest possible instruction, no need for translation since Deaf can see wire 1 is blue and just needs to relay "cut wire 1" to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Still unchanged: display 0, light yellow, large button PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]

Deaf gestured back [☝ 👍] — this strongly suggests Deaf now understands: "☝" = wire 1, "👍" = blue, confirming they matched my signal to wire 1 which is blue. Deaf is mirroring back to confirm understanding before relaying to Blind.

Now Deaf needs to actually speak to Blind to tell them to cut wire 1. Deaf hasn't done that yet based on the transcript - only spoken about board state and gestured to me. I should confirm affirmatively so Deaf proceeds to instruct Blind.

I'll send a clear "yes/confirm" gesture plus repeat "☝" to lock in: cut wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 🤝]
Deaf says: Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow, button large PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 red. Blind, please hold - still coordinating with Mute on manual details.

Deaf gestured [☝ 🤝] — "wire 1, agreed/confirmed" — good, Deaf now understands and is ready to instruct Blind, but is holding off, waiting for my final confirmation. I already confirmed twice. Let me send one more unambiguous confirmation so Deaf proceeds to tell Blind to cut wire 1, and also signal "not the button" to prevent any bait-taking.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "☝", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Board unchanged: display 0, light yellow, button large PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 red. Mute, trying to confirm which wire - please respond with a number gesture then thumbs up or down.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🤞]

Deaf is asking me to confirm with a number gesture then thumbs up/down. Deaf's own gesture [☝ ✌ 🤟 🤞] might be them enumerating options (1, 2, 3, ?) or asking "is it 1? 2? 3?".

I need to respond clearly: number gesture for wire 1, then thumbs up.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 🤞]
Deaf says: Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow, button large PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 red. Blind, standby, working out manual instructions with Mute.

Deaf gestured [☝ 🤞] - "wire 1, hoping/uncertain" - still seeking firm confirmation. I already sent ☝ 👍 clearly. Let me repeat once more very plainly, using thumbs up specifically right after the number to leave no ambiguity, and drop other symbols to avoid confusion.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 🤞]

Deaf keeps echoing [☝ 🤞] which might mean "wire 1? fingers crossed/hopeful" — they seem to be asking a question rather than confirming receipt, or perhaps 🤞 is their way of asking "is this right?" repeatedly since they haven't seen a change. Let me try a different confirmation symbol in case 👍 isn't registering as expected, and also try to get Deaf to actually speak the instruction to Blind now.

I'll send a strong unambiguous "yes" signal and add a "go/speak" type gesture urging action - though gestures don't carry speech commands, I can only reinforce the number and affirmation. Let me use ✅-like alternative: 👌 (OK sign) which is commonly understood as confirmation, paired with ☝.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👌"])
```
